# Specter Bridge

> Android-first native runtime and app tooling for web applications.

Specter Bridge serves a web app from an Android WebView and exposes explicitly registered native plugins through a request/response protocol. Ghost.js can build the web UI, while Specter Bridge supplies the Android host.

## Start here

- [README](README.md): current scope, requirements, quick start, and JavaScript API.
- [Architecture](docs/architecture.md): protocol, Android host, WebView security, Storage, and current limits.
- [CLI guide](docs/cli.md): `init`, `add`, `sync`, `build`, and `run` commands.
- [Ghost.js integration](docs/ghostjs-integration.md): use Ghost's mobile output as the Specter app's `webDir`.

## Packages

- `packages/core`: request IDs, timeouts, protocol handling, and plugin registration.
- `packages/plugin-storage`: browser fallback and Android app-private JSON storage API.
- `packages/cli`: project generator, Android template, asset sync, APK build, and install/run commands.

## Common commands

- `npm run specter -- init "My App" --app-id com.example.myapp`: create a starter app.
- `npx specter add android`: add the native Android project.
- `npx specter sync android`: copy the configured web output into the APK assets.
- `npx specter build android`: build a debug APK.
- `npx specter run android`: install and launch on one connected device or emulator.

## Current limits

Android is the only native host. iOS, permissions, camera/location, event messaging, and lifecycle APIs are not implemented. Storage is not encrypted. Native calls are restricted to the local asset origin and main frame.
